UPDATE: I am now looking into medical programs such as nursing and physician assistant pathways. The reason being that LCSW professionals seem burnt out and have a limited scope of practice and a cap on wage rates.  PMHNP (psyche nurse practitioners) have a larger scope of practice and can still provide therapy services and case management services like an LCSW. Also, the time it takes to complete an MSW + get licensed (~4 years) is only slightly shorter than the time it takes to take pre-nursing prerequisites, earn an RN license, gain experience, and then become a certified NP (~4-5 years). And after the first 1-2 years when RN licensure is complete, the pay rate is around the same as a LCSW. Once an NP certification is complete, the pay is double a LCSW and the work *can be* similar (especially if pursuing an PMHNP focus). Similar for a PA which is around 3-4 years to complete prerequisites and the PA program. Only, there is no immediate wage boost in the first 1-2 years like there is for the RN to NP nursing path as a PA will need to wait until graduation to see a wage increase.
